**A Dynamic Island for your Android punch-hole camera — running over every app on the phone.**

A system overlay that turns the camera cutout into a live pill: at rest it is a circle around the hole, indistinguishable from the cutout itself. Something happens, it grows out of the hole to show you; the moment passes, it shrinks back and disappears.

> **A newer release is available.** See [v2.7.0](https://github.com/lhetvillanueva2000-maker/Dynamic-camera-punch/releases/tag/v2.7.0), which rebuilds the control panel.

> If a download will not install, check its size first. A phone browser that lands on a GitHub *page* rather than the file saves an HTML error page under the `.apk` name, and the installer then reports the APK as corrupt.

## New in 2.6.0

### Three tabs

The control panel became three panes with a sliding indicator: **Cards** (what the island shows), **Look** (how it looks and moves), **Settings** (you, your device, support).

### Seventeen dials, over a live preview

Position on both axes, compact corner radius, expanded radius and width, idle scale, opacity at rest, border width, background and outline colour, shadow strength, animation speed, bounce, reduce-animation, glow, whether an arriving notification lands minimised or already open, and how long an alert stays up — plus the cutout shape.

A live preview loops idle → compact → expanded with the current settings, so a dial's effect is visible without leaving the screen. Sliders update cheaply while dragging and commit on release, so adjusting one does not thrash the overlay redrawing behind the app.

### Presets with your own names

Save the whole Look tab as "Night" or "Discreet" and switch in one tap. Stored as JSON, so a dial added in a later version needs no migration — unknown keys are ignored and missing ones fall back to their defaults.

### Assignable gestures

Tap, double tap, long press, swipe left and swipe right, each settable to: open the app, expand, collapse, dismiss, swap, play/pause, next track, previous track, or nothing.

Double tap defaults to *nothing* deliberately — with nothing bound to it a single tap can act the moment you lift your finger, instead of waiting to find out whether a second tap is coming. Assignments are stored by name rather than by position in a menu, so a later version inserting an action cannot silently remap an existing binding.

### CPU and storage, alongside RAM

Total/available/used RAM, used and free storage, and the chipset with its core count.

The CPU figure is the app's own share of wall-clock time, and the card says so. A live system-wide CPU percentage has not been readable by an ordinary Android app since `/proc/stat` was restricted in Android 8 — anything showing one without root is a system app.

### A bundled support page

Opened from Settings and running in a separate process, so it costs nothing while closed. It makes no network requests at all, which is the only way it could work in an app that declares no `INTERNET` permission.

> The page ships without a QR image. Drop a `donate-qr.png` into `android/app/src/main/assets/support/` and rebuild to add one.

## Requirements

Android 7.0 (API 24) or later · targetSdk 34 · about 168 KB on disk · working set 30–45 MB · six permissions, no `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`, no `INTERNET`.

## Known limitations

- Some manufacturer skins — notably Xiaomi/MIUI and some Huawei builds — add their own extra "show on top" toggle and aggressively kill background services. If the island vanishes after a while, the app has to be exempted in the vendor's battery manager.
- This build has not been run on physical hardware. It compiles clean and passes Android Lint with zero errors, but that is not the same as a device test.
